column2: An earlier protection arrangement placed the Basotho kingdom under British authority before the settlement of 1868. The premature arrangement is withdrawn. Moshoeshoe retains his own government until the later appeal for protection is considered.
Establish the Free State frontier administration.

The Free State is establishing a frontier settlement at Ladybrand in 1867, named for the mother of President Johannes Brand. The district has become part of the struggle over the land west of the Basotho heartland. British possession created by the earlier protection arrangement is corrected here in favour of the Orange Free State, the later Aliwal North agreement will settle the frontier diplomatically.

The settlement of 1869 defines the boundary between the Orange Free State and British-protected Basutoland. Ladybrand remains on the Free State side. Basotho government continues in the protected territory, while the disputed western districts are administered by the republic.
The kingdom survives under British protection.

Moshoeshoe's repeated appeals have brought British recognition of the Basotho as protected subjects. The proclamation of 12 March 1868 places the remaining kingdom under the Crown. Its government and land remain together, Ladybrand is outside this protected territory. British intervention ends the immediate conflict with the Orange Free State and establishes a new diplomatic frontier.

Responsibility for Basutoland passes to the Cape administration in 1871. The change places local disputes, revenue and policing under colonial officials while Basotho institutions continue within the British protection arrangement. The balance between colonial demands and chiefly authority will become increasingly contested.

Following the conflict over Cape rule and disarmament, responsibility for Basutoland returns to direct British administration in 1884. The new arrangement preserves the protected territory and recognises that the Cape experiment has failed. Local government remains within the Basotho kingdom rather than being dispersed among neighbouring colonial districts.
End the fighting and preserve the protected kingdom.
Settlement of the Basotho Gun War

The attempt to impose disarmament has met sustained resistance. A negotiated settlement ends the fighting while preserving British protection and Basotho local government. The failures of Cape administration remain unresolved and will lead to a return to direct Crown administration in 1884.
Klein Vrystaat Joins the South African Republic

The small republic established in 1886 has reached an agreement to enter the South African Republic. Its separate administration is to be absorbed in 1891, bringing the district and its inhabitants under the wider republic. The transfer concerns Klein Vrystaat itself, rather than the whole neighbouring Swazi district.
Demand Nkomazi alone, enforce the claim if refused.
Demand the four eastern districts and an outlet to the sea.
The Eastern Frontier and the Road to the Sea

The union of the Transvaal districts has renewed debate over the eastern frontier. Gaza authority reaches into Nkomazi and along the routes toward the coast. A narrow settlement would seek recognition of the republic's claim to Nkomazi alone. A much wider ultimatum would demand Lepelle, Manjacaze and Inkomati as well, bringing an ocean outlet within reach but placing the republic on a course of expansion beyond its inland frontier. Gaza is a negotiating power with interests of its own, refusal may bring war.
Reject the demand, prepare to defend the frontier.

Envoys from the South African Republic demand a settlement limited to Nkomazi. Acceptance would draw a new frontier while preserving the remainder of Gaza's territory. Refusal risks a war over the district. The government must weigh the cost of conceding this claim against the danger and expense of resisting it.
Reject the demand, prepare to defend the frontier.

The South African Republic demands the Gaza-held districts of Nkomazi, Lepelle, Manjacaze and Inkomati. Acceptance would relinquish valuable territory and routes toward the coast. Refusal leaves the dispute to the commandos and Gaza's defenders. Territory held by another power cannot be ceded by our administration.

Gaza has refused the territorial demand. The volksraad's ultimatum now commits the republic to enforce its claim by arms. The war settlement is limited to the specified districts held by Gaza, victory will not annex the Gaza Empire or transfer the possessions of another power.

Record the agreement and administer the new districts.

Gaza has accepted the demand and transferred the agreed territory. Nkomazi is recognised as part of the South African Republic. The wider settlement, if demanded, concerns only the listed districts that Gaza actually held, another power's possessions remain outside this agreement.

Moshoeshoe has appealed for British protection from the wars with the Orange Free State. On 12 March 1868 the Crown can recognise the remaining Basotho kingdom as protected territory. The arrangement preserves the kingdom and ends the immediate fighting. It does not annex Ladybrand or disperse the other Basotho districts among British possessions.
Proclaim British protection over the Basotho kingdom.

Stellaland and Goshen have agreed to unite their small frontier republics in August 1883. A shared government at Vryburg is intended to strengthen their administration and bargaining position. The two districts will retain their local communities while entering a single state, whose existence remains contested by the neighbouring African rulers and the British authorities.
The separate Klein Vrystaat district follows its own republican settlement.

Cape efforts to disarm the Basotho have provoked resistance. The question is whether colonial authority can compel the surrender of weapons without breaking the protection settlement. Fighting would suspend the existing subject relationship while British and Cape forces attempt to restore authority over the kingdom.
Enforce disarmament and restore colonial authority.
Withdraw the demand and preserve the peace.
The Cape administers the protected Basotho territory, creating friction over local authority and colonial policy.
